You describe people’s personalities and master SER / ESTAR at an advanced level, including the adjectives that change their meaning.
Javier is very nice, but today he’s serious.
The party is at my place.
To describe someone’s personality with SER.
To describe temporary states and changes with ESTAR.
To use the adjectives that change their meaning: listo, aburrido, rico, malo…
To use ESTAR + participle for results: está cerrado, está roto.
To know the exception: events “take place” with SER (la fiesta es en…).
Lucía has a new boyfriend, Javier. Ana is dying to know everything.
Right, tell me. What’s Javier like?
He’s tall, dark-haired… and very good-looking. He’s from Valencia and he’s an architect.
And his personality? What’s he like?
He’s very funny and generous. And he’s very clever: he speaks four languages.
Great! And doesn’t he have any faults?
Well… sometimes he’s a bit serious. And he’s very tidy: his flat is always perfect.
That’s not a fault, that’s a miracle! How is he at the moment? Is he happy with his job?
This week he’s very stressed: he’s finishing a huge project.
And yesterday he was a bit ill, with a temperature. That’s why he didn’t come to dinner.
Poor thing! Listen, on Saturday it’s Mihai’s birthday party. It’s at my place. Will you come?
Of course! That way you’ll meet him. But I’m warning you: at first he seems shy.
Don’t worry. With Mum’s food, everyone is happy. The cocido is going to be delicious!
Ha, ha. Are you ready to meet your future brother-in-law?
Simpático, antipático, fantástico: the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable.
Caro (expensive) / carro (cart, car in Latin America). Pero (but) / perro (dog).
1. Review: SER = what you are like, ESTAR = how you are
change: Está muy delgado (he’s lost weight).
origin, job: Es de Valencia, es arquitecto.
material, possession: Es de madera. Es mío.
the result of an action: Está roto.
time, date: Son las tres. Es lunes.
an action in progress: Está trabajando.
A useful question: “Is it part of what the person or thing IS?” → SER. “Is it how they ARE right now?” → ESTAR.
Here is the A2 trap: some adjectives have two different meanings with SER and with ESTAR!
The film is boring, and I’m bored.
“Estoy aburrido” = I’m bored (now). “Soy aburrido” = I’m a boring person! Be careful what you say about yourself…
When you describe the state that results from an action, you use ESTAR + participle. The participle agrees like an adjective:
The difference from chapter 13: “He cerrado la puerta” (I have closed the door = the action) versus “La puerta está cerrada” (the door is closed = the state).
You learned that place is expressed with ESTAR. But when you talk about where events TAKE PLACE (a party, a concert, a meeting), you use SER!
The party is (takes place) at my house.
The concert is at the stadium.
My house is in the centre. (a place, not an event → ESTAR)
Trick: if you can say “takes place”, use SER.

And some useful verbs: parecer (to seem): Parece simpático. Llevarse bien / mal con (to get on well / badly with): Me llevo muy bien con mi hermana.
To be tactful, Spaniards use diminutives or “un poco”: “Es un poco tímido” is nicer than “Es tímido”.
El concierto está en el estadio.
El concierto es en el estadio.
I get on very well with my sister.

Pablo describes the members of his family: what they’re like and how they’ve been lately.
My mother, Carmen, is the most generous person I know. She’s always thinking of others.
Lately she’s been a bit worried because Dad has back problems.
My father, Juan, seems serious on the outside, but he’s actually very funny.
He’s been retired for two years and he’s calmer now than ever.
My sister Ana is very hard-working and a bit of a perfectionist. But since she met Mihai she’s much more relaxed.
Lucía, the youngest, is the funniest in the family. She’s never bored.
Right now she’s madly in love with a guy from Valencia. She’s on cloud nine!
My wife, Elena, is very honest: if she doesn’t like something, she tells you.
This month she’s very tired because the children are ill.
And me… I’m the calmest of them all. Well, that’s what my wife says. My children say I’m boring.
But that’s not true: I’m calm, not boring!
“estar en las nubes” = to have your head in the clouds / be on cloud nine
Juan está malo de la espalda
Ana and Lucía are sisters, but everyone says they’re nothing alike.
Ana has long dark hair and brown eyes. She’s serious, tidy and very hard-working.
She’s always on time, always has a plan and never forgets a birthday.
Lucía is blonde, with short curly hair and green eyes. She’s funny, spontaneous and a bit messy.
She’s late everywhere, changes her plans every five minutes and never knows where her keys are.
When they were little, they argued a lot. Ana was the older sister and was always worried about Lucía.
Lucía was the youngest and was always fed up with Ana’s advice.
But now, as adults, they get on very well. They talk on the phone every day and tell each other all their secrets.
This week, though, something is different. Lucía is very nervous: her wedding to Javier is a month away and she has nothing ready.
The dress isn’t finished, the invitations haven’t been sent and the restaurant isn’t confirmed.
One evening Lucía called Ana in tears. “I’m not going to manage it all,” she said. “I’m a disaster.”
Ana arrived at her flat half an hour later with a notebook, a pen and a box of cakes.
“You’re not a disaster,” she told her. “You’re creative. I’m organised. Together we’re perfect.”
For three hours they made lists. Ana organised the dates and phone numbers. Lucía designed some gorgeous invitations with hand-drawn pictures.
By midnight everything was ready. Lucía was calm for the first time in weeks.
“Thank you, sis,” she said. “You’re the most boring and the most wonderful person in the world.”
Ana laughed. “And you’re the messiest… By the way, aren’t these your keys?” They were in the box of cakes.
A month later the wedding day came. Everything went perfectly: the dress was ready, the invitations had arrived on time and the restaurant was full of flowers.
There was just one small problem: ten minutes before the ceremony, Lucía couldn’t find the rings. Ana calmly took them out of her bag. “Just in case,” she said with a wink.
Lucía and Javier danced all night. For once, Ana got home late too.
“estar aburrida de” = to be fed up with
“falta un mes” = it’s a month away
